report.source_text: Postoperatively, child recovered well and was discharged with a corked tracheostomy tube and nasal breathing. Follow-up endoscopic evaluation at 2 months did not suggest cyst recurrence. Delayed decannulation following exclusion of recurrence has been planned to ensure avoidance of any emergent visit to hospital during the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic and nation-wide lockdown.

clinician.trajectory_summary: An 18-month-old girl born preterm with 1 month of neonatal intubation presented with progressive noisy breathing and stridor over several months, acutely worsened over 1 week following fever and diarrhea. On initial presentation, she was irritable with tachypnea, tachycardia, and biphasic stridor with suprasternal and intercostal retraction that worsened on crying and was not relieved by positional changes. History of multiple hospitalizations for croup without complete symptomatic relief raised suspicion for structural airway lesion. COVID-19 test was negative. Contrast-enhanced CT of the neck revealed a 9×8 mm hypodense, non-enhancing lesion in the subglottis. Direct laryngoscopy confirmed a submucosal cystic lesion immediately beneath the mobile vocal cords arising from the right posterolateral wall of the subglottis with no significant patent airway around the cyst. The cyst was aspirated (yielding 1 mL of thick yellowish clear fluid) and marsupialised using coblator. Tracheotomy was performed with mask ventilation. Postoperatively, the child recovered well and was discharged with a corked tracheostomy tube and nasal breathing. Follow-up endoscopic evaluation at 2 months showed no cyst recurrence. Delayed decannulation was planned.
